records.title: Iranian strikes on Bahrain and continuing attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz
records.location: Bahrain; Strait of Hormuz and Gulf of Oman approaches
records.summary: On 21 November 2026 an Iranian attack hit a civilian industrial facility in Bahrain, injuring two people, one critically, according to Bahrain's Interior Ministry. Iran's Revolutionary Guards said they targeted US military positions in the kingdom, which hosts the US Navy's Fifth Fleet. The strike comes amid a sustained campaign against commercial shipping in and around the Strait of Hormuz, where UKMTO has logged repeated projectile strikes on tankers in November. This matters because the Strait carries a large share of world oil and LNG trade and attacks on Gulf states risk widening the war.

confirmed_facts.text: Bahrain's Interior Ministry said an Iranian attack on 21 November hit a civilian industrial facility, causing a fire and material damage.
Two people were injured: a Pakistani resident in critical condition and a Bahraini citizen in stable condition (Interior Ministry).

UKMTO reported that on 16 November a tanker transiting outbound through the Strait of Hormuz was struck by an unidentified projectile, causing an engine-room fire; a second tanker attack the same day left a vessel disabled.

reported_claims.text: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said the 21 November strikes targeted US military positions in Bahrain.
The IRGC claimed that several tankers using a route it had not authorised struck mines and caught fire or sank in mid-November; these sinkings have not been independently verified.

international_perspectives.text: Bahrain's Foreign Ministry rejected the IRGC justification and said the strike hit an exclusively civilian industrial site.
Saudi Arabia and Jordan condemned the attack on Bahrain.

records.impact_assessment: Observed: casualties and fire damage at an industrial site in Bahrain; repeated strikes on tankers with engine-room fires and at least one disabled vessel. Potential: further disruption to Gulf energy exports and shipping insurance, attacks on desalination, power or port infrastructure in Gulf states, and escalation involving US forces.
records.priority_rationale: CRITICAL: active armed attacks by a state on a neighbouring state and on commercial shipping, confirmed by official statements and independent maritime reporting, with a direct effect on a global energy chokepoint.
unknowns: Exact location and identity of the industrial facility hit in Bahrain
Number of vessels actually sunk, as opposed to IRGC claims
Whether US–Iran indirect talks will produce a de-escalation
reassessment_triggers: Resumption of large-scale US strikes on Iran
A verified sinking with loss of life
A negotiated reopening of the Strait
monitoring_actions: Track UKMTO warnings and JMIC advisories for the Strait of Hormuz
Follow Bahrain Interior Ministry statements
Watch Gulf desalination, power and port operators for disruption notices

records.title: Russian Kh-101 cruise missiles land in Poland during attacks on Ukraine
records.location: Nowy Lipowiec, Rudnik nad Sanem and Mołodycz, south-eastern Poland
records.summary: Early on 20 November 2026, during large-scale Russian strikes on Ukraine, three objects came down in south-eastern Poland, a NATO member. Polish prosecutors have since said all three were Russian Kh-101 cruise missiles. No one was hurt. Poland's prime minister called it a likely provocation timed to European military exercises nearby, and NATO's Secretary-General called it a grave violation of Polish airspace.

confirmed_facts.text: Objects struck three locations in south-eastern Poland on 20 November: Nowy Lipowiec, Rudnik nad Sanem and Mołodycz.
Polish prosecutors said on 23 November that all three objects were Russian Kh-101 cruise missiles; no injuries or infrastructure damage were reported.
NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte called the incident a grave violation of Poland's airspace.

reported_claims.text: Prime Minister Donald Tusk said the incident was likely a provocation timed to European military exercises in Poland.

international_perspectives.text: Ukraine's foreign minister said the incident shows the threat Russian aggression poses to Europe as a whole.

records.impact_assessment: Observed: missile impacts on NATO territory without casualties. Potential: further airspace violations, pressure for stronger air defence along NATO's eastern flank, and escalation risk if an impact causes casualties.
records.priority_rationale: HIGH: confirmed weapons impacts on NATO territory with clear escalation potential, but no casualties or damage.
unknowns: Whether the missiles were deliberately aimed at Poland or strayed
Whether a Russian explanation will be offered
monitoring_actions: Follow Polish prosecutors' and Defence Ministry statements
Watch NATO statements on eastern-flank air defence

records.title: Russian ballistic missile strike on central Kryvyi Rih kills two, wounds 60
records.summary: A Russian strike on the centre of Kryvyi Rih late on 20 November 2026 killed a seven-year-old boy and a 20-year-old woman and wounded 60 people, including six children, according to local officials. About 25 apartment buildings, a hospital, schools and businesses were damaged. The strike was part of continuing large-scale Russian attacks on Ukrainian cities and energy infrastructure.

confirmed_facts.text: The strike killed two people, a seven-year-old boy and a 20-year-old woman, and wounded 60, including six children (local officials).
About 25 apartment buildings, a hospital, schools and businesses were damaged.

records.impact_assessment: Observed: civilian deaths and injuries and damage to housing, a hospital and schools. Potential: continued strikes on civilian areas and energy infrastructure during winter.
records.priority_rationale: HIGH: confirmed lethal strike on a city centre as part of an ongoing interstate war; localised rather than a change in the war's overall course.
unknowns: Exact munitions used and intended target
monitoring_actions: Track Ukrainian regional administration casualty updates
Watch for strikes on energy infrastructure ahead of winter

records.title: Suspected Ukrainian sea-drone strike damages Russian corvette at Benghazi naval base
records.summary: On 22 November 2026 the Russian navy corvette Merkury, docked at the Benghazi Naval Base in eastern Libya, was hit by what Libyan officials described as a Ukrainian sea drone; a cargo ship was hit in a second attack hours later. Two Libyan military officials told the Associated Press the corvette was severely damaged and a fire broke out. President Zelenskyy hailed the attack and claimed the ship was sunk. The incident extends the Russia–Ukraine war into North Africa.

reported_claims.text: Two Libyan military officials said the strike severely damaged the corvette Merkury and set a fire at the base.
A cargo ship was also hit by a sea drone in a second attack hours later.
President Zelenskyy said Ukrainian sea drones sank the Russian warship.

records.impact_assessment: Observed: damage to a Russian warship and a fire at a naval base in a third country. Potential: further attacks on Russian assets in the Mediterranean and Libya, risk to Libyan port operations and shipping, and friction with eastern Libyan authorities.
records.priority_rationale: HIGH: a significant geographic extension of an interstate war onto a third country's territory. Evidence is Reported because all accounts trace to one wire chain (AP) and Ukraine's claim of a sinking conflicts with Libyan officials' account.
unknowns: Whether the corvette sank or was damaged
Casualties
Launch point of the drones
reassessment_triggers: Independent imagery confirming the ship's status
monitoring_actions: Watch for Russian and Libyan National Army statements
Track further incidents at Libyan ports

records.title: Global cyber campaign against industrial refrigeration and cold-chain systems
records.location: Retail grocery, cold storage, transport and healthcare cold chains
records.summary: On 5 November 2026 CISA, the FBI, HHS, USDA and the Department of Transportation issued a joint fact sheet warning of malicious cyber activity targeting industrial refrigeration and cold-chain monitoring systems globally. Attackers are exploiting unpatched or internet-accessible temperature controllers and refrigeration management systems. The warning followed compromises of supermarket refrigeration in France and other European countries in October that forced stock to be destroyed.

confirmed_facts.text: CISA, the FBI, HHS, USDA and DOT published a joint TLP:CLEAR fact sheet on 5 November urging owners to harden industrial refrigeration and cold-chain monitoring systems.
The agencies said successful exploitation could change temperatures and cause fire hazards, loss of inventory and equipment damage.

reported_claims.text: In October, refrigeration controllers at an estimated 250 to 350 French supermarkets were compromised, with attackers activating defrost functions and raising temperatures.
Supermarket chains in France and elsewhere in Europe destroyed food stock after systems administered by a refrigeration provider were compromised.

records.impact_assessment: Observed: food stock destroyed at European supermarkets. Potential: spoilage of food and temperature-sensitive medicine, fire hazards and equipment damage across food, agriculture, transport and healthcare cold chains.
records.priority_rationale: HIGH: confirmed, ongoing activity against systems with physical consequences across several critical sectors, documented by five US agencies; the actors are not publicly identified.
unknowns: Identity and motive of the actors
Specific vulnerabilities exploited
Number of organisations affected outside Europe
reassessment_triggers: Reported harm to medicine or blood supplies
A CVE or KEV listing for an exploited controller
monitoring_actions: Inventory internet-exposed refrigeration and temperature controllers
Check ThreatWatch for exploited controller vulnerabilities
Follow CISA and CERT-FR updates

records.title: Sudanese army offensive against RSF in West Kordofan drives new displacement
records.location: West Kordofan (El Khuwai, Al Nahud axis) and Blue Nile, Sudan
records.summary: The Sudanese army and allied forces have advanced against the Rapid Support Forces in West Kordofan in November 2026, seizing El Khuwai and pushing toward Al Nahud with drone strikes. Thousands of civilians have fled, and more than 51,000 people were reported newly displaced in Blue Nile. A rights monitor accused the RSF of killing civilians in the Abu Qalb area.

reported_claims.text: Army and allied troops seized several areas around El Khuwai on 13 November after clashes with the RSF.
Army drones carried out intensive strikes on RSF positions across West Kordofan on 15 November, and thousands of civilians fled westward toward Darfur.
More than 51,000 people were newly displaced in Blue Nile, and about 2,100 fled Abu Zabad.
The Kordofan Monitor accused RSF gunmen of killing civilians in the Abu Qalb area.

records.impact_assessment: Observed: large-scale displacement and civilian killings. Potential: a renewed humanitarian emergency in Kordofan, further drone warfare, and spillover toward Darfur.
records.priority_rationale: HIGH: active large-scale fighting with significant civilian displacement in one of the world's largest humanitarian crises; front-line claims come mainly from one side, so evidence is Reported.
unknowns: Civilian casualty totals
Independent verification of territorial claims
reassessment_triggers: UN OCHA or IOM displacement figures
monitoring_actions: Track OCHA and IOM displacement updates
Watch for RSF statements and counter-claims

records.title: Large unannounced Chinese naval exercise around Taiwan and the western Pacific
records.location: Western Pacific between Taiwan and Guam
records.summary: In early November 2026 more than 100 Chinese navy and coast guard vessels, including two aircraft carriers, operated in the western Pacific around Taiwan in an exercise Beijing did not announce, according to Taiwan's National Security Council. A senior Taiwan security official told Reuters the drills included simulated attacks and were larger than China's 'Justice Mission 2025' exercise. US analysts assessed it may have simulated isolating Taiwan.

reported_claims.text: More than 100 PLA Navy and China Coast Guard vessels were operating in the western Pacific, including the Liaoning and Fujian carrier groups.
The deployment was larger than 'Justice Mission 2025' and included simulated attacks on other militaries and cities including Taiwan's.

international_perspectives.text: The Institute for the Study of War and AEI assessed the activity as a possible major exercise simulating the isolation of Taiwan.
Officials in Taipei described the drills as 'silent intimidation' ahead of major international meetings.

records.impact_assessment: Observed: a large-scale naval deployment without public announcement. Potential: shorter warning times for any real blockade, and pressure on shipping and regional militaries.
records.priority_rationale: HIGH: a credible, large military activity relevant to a potential blockade of a major economy; China has not publicly described the exercise, so evidence is Reported.
unknowns: Beijing's stated purpose
Whether vessels have fully returned to port
monitoring_actions: Follow Taiwan Ministry of National Defense daily reports
Track ISW/AEI China–Taiwan updates

records.title: Attackers begin using autonomous AI agents to find and exploit vulnerabilities
records.location: Global; observed against organisations in Asia
records.summary: On 16 November 2026 Google Threat Intelligence Group and Mandiant reported, for the first time, threat actors using an AI agent framework to automate vulnerability discovery and exploitation without a human in the loop. Amazon separately disclosed that autonomous agents found and exploited a previously unknown vulnerability against universities in East Asia, and a US GAO report said AI agents have begun carrying out cyberattacks with minimal human direction. The window between a patch and its exploitation is shrinking.

confirmed_facts.text: Google's GTIG AI Threat Tracker, published 16 November, describes the first case Google has seen of attackers fully automating vulnerability discovery and exploitation with an LLM-based framework.

reported_claims.text: Amazon Threat Intelligence disclosed on 20 November that autonomous AI agents discovered and exploited a previously unknown vulnerability during an intrusion campaign against universities in East Asia; a human operator supplied targets and the objective.
reported_claims.attributed_to: Amazon Threat Intelligence (as reported by Digital Watch)

reported_claims.text: The vulnerability Amazon described is a path traversal in MONAI Label, a medical-imaging annotation server (CVE-2026-133968, affecting versions through 0.8.5); the CVE record states it was exploited in the wild from September 2026.
reported_claims.attributed_to: Cloud Security Alliance; CVE record via VulDB

reported_claims.text: A Government Accountability Office report released 20 November found autonomous AI agents have begun carrying out cyberattacks with minimal human direction.
reported_claims.attributed_to: US GAO (as reported by The Washington Times)

international_perspectives.text: Google warned that unsophisticated near-autonomous attacks could become common within about three months.

records.impact_assessment: Observed: automated patch-to-exploit activity and AI-agent intrusions. Potential: much faster exploitation of newly patched flaws, forcing shorter patch cycles across all sectors.
records.priority_rationale: HIGH: a confirmed change in attacker capability reported by major security vendors and a US government auditor, with broad cross-sector exposure.
unknowns: Operators behind the frameworks
Success rate of autonomous exploitation
Whether fully autonomous zero-day attacks against real targets are already occurring
reassessment_triggers: A confirmed fully autonomous intrusion with significant impact
monitoring_actions: Shorten patch windows for internet-facing systems
Use ThreatWatch to track newly exploited CVEs daily
Follow GTIG and Amazon threat intelligence publications

records.title: COP31 climate talks in Antalya collapse without a deal
records.summary: The UN climate conference COP31 in Antalya ended on 22 November 2026 without an overarching agreement after the European Union and others rejected a final draft they said was too weak, notably because it did not mention fossil fuels. It was the longest COP on record and the first major breakdown since Copenhagen in 2009, leaving climate finance and adaptation commitments unresolved.

confirmed_facts.text: COP31 ended on 22 November without consensus on its main cover decision.
The EU and others rejected the final draft, which made no mention of fossil fuels.

international_perspectives.text: Delegates from developing countries said the failure left out many things they wanted, including progress on finance.

records.impact_assessment: Potential: slower climate-finance flows to vulnerable countries and weaker coordination on disaster response, increasing long-term environmental and humanitarian security risk.
records.priority_rationale: MODERATE: a confirmed multilateral breakdown with long-term security implications but no immediate physical harm.
monitoring_actions: Track UNFCCC statements on next steps

records.title: Guatemala declares 30-day state of siege in Zacapa and Izabal after armed attacks
records.summary: Guatemala's government declared a 30-day state of siege in the eastern departments of Zacapa and Izabal on 14 November 2026 (Government Decree 8-2026) after armed attacks linked to drug-trafficking groups, deploying about 400 soldiers to Zacapa and 600 to Izabal. Congress ratified the measure on 17 November and authorised security forces to take control of prisons nationwide. The interior minister has said an extension to other departments could be considered.

confirmed_facts.text: Government Decree 8-2026 declared a 30-day state of siege in Zacapa and Izabal from 14 November.
Congress ratified the measure on 17 November with 147 votes and authorised security forces to take control of prisons nationwide.

reported_claims.text: Two armed attacks on 13 November left seven people dead.
The interior minister said the government could analyse extending the state of siege to other departments.

records.impact_assessment: Observed: military deployment and restricted civil liberties in two departments. Potential: displacement of criminal activity to other areas and wider emergency measures.
records.priority_rationale: MODERATE: a confirmed national security emergency measure with regional drug-trafficking implications but geographically contained.
unknowns: Whether violence has declined since the deployment
monitoring_actions: Track government and Congress decisions on extension
Watch violence indicators in neighbouring departments
